title: Loss of plasticity: paper evidence, CBP code, and limits for the integration study
scope: Read-only research note; no extra experiment or frozen runtime change

paper.title: Loss of plasticity in deep continual learning
paper.access_note: Publisher HTML/PDF redirected to an inaccessible Nature login endpoint. The paper text, Fig. 1 caption and extended discussion were read through indexed PMC full text, an official primary-article mirror.

evidence.claim: Sequences of binary ImageNet tasks measure held-out accuracy after training each new class pair. Thirty runs report means and standard errors.
Standard backpropagation loses new-task performance across many step sizes by about 2,000 tasks. CBP, L2 and Shrink and Perturb continue over 5,000 tasks.
Future learning differs from old-task retention. The authors explicitly say current CBP does not solve forgetting; utility focuses on current data.

Empirical degradation and mitigation are not universal impossibility or indefinite-success theorems. Fig. 1 does not test persistent recurrent-state memory, long-wait control or biological equivalence.

official_implementation.snapshot_scope: Current official repository snapshot, not asserted to be the exact 2024 publication commit

sources.evidence: The paper implementations are cbp.py, convCBP.py and res_gnt.py. Newer CBPLinear/CBPConv wrappers are explicitly described as less thoroughly tested; these are not interchangeable reproduction claims.
learn performs a labelled forward pass, loss.backward, optimizer.step, then generate-and-test. CBP augments backpropagation; it is not a forward-only learning rule.

Activity/weight statistics estimate unit utility with EMA bias correction. The adaptable-contribution option scales outgoing-weight magnitude times centred absolute activity by inverse incoming-weight magnitude. Mature units with lowest estimated utility are selected at a small accumulated replacement rate. Incoming weights are randomly reinitialized; outgoing weights and ages are zeroed. AdamGnT-specific optimizer entries are reset; do not assume every optimizer variant receives identical treatment.

The checked ImageNet config selects adaptable_contribution, SGD with momentum, replacement_rate=3e-4, maturity_threshold=100 and decay_rate=0.99. These are paper-repository settings, not settings adopted by our experiment.

comparison_with_current_rule.classification: Own analysis from the inspected code, not a claim established by the Nature experiments
comparison_with_current_rule.cbp: Ranks units using current-use utility, temporarily protects immature units and injects random features through replacement. It neither permanently protects all useful historical units nor directly solves forgetting.
comparison_with_current_rule.temporal_oja: Maintains a per-actor activity EMA in physical time and applies dense recurrent-weight updates proportional to post-activity outer lagged pre-activity minus a post-squared weight decay. It has no unit ranking, maturity gate, replacement or random feature generation.
comparison_with_current_rule.shared_limit: Activity statistics are heuristic signals. Neither a CBP utility score nor this Oja-like coactivity proves a unit is globally important to all past tasks.
comparison_with_current_rule.continuous_state_limit: Porting unit replacement to this recurrent controller would require an explicit policy for recurrent rows/columns, encoder/head connections, Adam state, live h and local q. Feed-forward CBP supplies no guarantee that such surgery preserves concurrent unfinished requests.
comparison_with_current_rule.credit_limit: Our supervised hybrids still receive temporal credit through truncated BPTT. The local trace is activity, not a loss derivative or e-prop eligibility trace; its Oja-style name does not confer linear stationary PCA guarantees.
comparison_with_current_rule.current_study_limit: Frozen long-wait errors, forgetting old conditions and slower acquisition are different measurements. The present fixed-exposure stage is not by itself a repeated equal-difficulty new-task plasticity benchmark.

future_measurements.proposal: Read-only activity health at fixed checkpoints
future_measurements.details: On complete frozen own-action forks, report centred activation variance, covariance spectrum/effective or stable rank, and tanh derivative/saturation distributions. Balance active/idle phases and task ages; use fixed thresholds and independent training seeds. A quiet idle unit is not automatically dormant, and ReLU dead-unit thresholds do not transfer directly to tanh.

In detached shadow copies, measure loss-gradient norms and layerwise proposed/actual update-to-weight ratios on matched causal data; retain existing Adam/local update counters. Separate optimizer scale, saturation and representation collapse. Do not update production weights or interpret a large gradient as proof of useful learning.

future_measurements.proposal: Future learning-curve challenge under a separate frozen protocol
future_measurements.details: At several saved life stages, fork full state into matched frozen and learning branches facing the same specified new regime. Compare loss reduction and held-out own-action clean completion per fixed examples, gradient updates and local writes. Across life stages, report changed request populations; never attach an arbitrary fresh world to old h. Measure old-condition retention separately.

Collect current-versus-old-data unit-use scores without replacing units, alongside cue/first-legal readability transitions and inactive-action histories. If replacement is later tested, preregister random-replacement and norm/shrink controls plus disruption of in-flight requests, optimizer state and auxiliary trace handling. No such intervention is part of the current 12 arms.

formal_results: Intentionally omitted; this note does not report unfinished main-study outcomes
